children.default: No monitoring in place usually means you're relying on filter logs to surface concerns. These logs provide almost no context for DSLs, and filters (by their design) cannot see a majority of safeguarding risks that appear online. The information is sporadic, incomplete and leaves DSLs at a loss as to what they need to do next.

default.text_below: No monitoring in place usually means you're relying on filter logs to surface concerns. These logs provide almost no context for DSLs, and filters (by their design) cannot see a majority of safeguarding risks that appear online. The information is sporadic, incomplete and leaves DSLs at a loss as to what they need to do next.

children.default: Unmoderated monitoring uses technology to identify risks beyond what a web filter can see. This improves visibility of risks and can provide more insight on individual concerns. However, these systems produce huge numbers of false positives - meaning DSLs waste a lot of time sifting through alerts to identify which are real.

However, these systems produce huge numbers of false positives - meaning DSLs waste a lot of time sifting through alerts to identify which are real.

children.default: With human-moderated monitoring, trained moderators review alerts and remove false positives before they reach your school. This protects DSL workloads and ensures they get straight to the genuine alerts they need to see. If a student's health or life is at risk, your team is contacted directly by phone - supporting fast interventions.
